---
title: "Publication Gates"
page-type: project
audience: "Publishers, approvers, reviewers, and maintainers"
status: "Required before publication"
---

No report or alert becomes publishable merely because it renders, validates against a schema, passes a comparison, or appears in a Snapshot Output Bundle. Publication requires all applicable gates below.

## Privacy

- Classify facility-level, child-impact, geospatial, identity, source, and operational fields for the intended audience.
- Publish only allowlisted metadata and outputs; keep ProductFactSet, raw evidence, private contacts, recipients, and delivery state internal.
- Inspect actual HTML and PNG content for embedded sensitive data, remote resources, unsafe metadata, and unintended precision.
- Document retention, redaction, aggregation, sharing, and deletion rules.

## Accessibility

- Verify heading structure, table semantics, meaningful link text, keyboard navigation, and language metadata.
- Provide useful alternative text and non-visual equivalents for maps and charts.
- Check contrast, color-independent meaning, zoom, reflow, mobile widths, and low-bandwidth behavior in a real browser.
- Treat automated scans as a baseline, not proof of accessibility.

## Certification

- Preserve the distinction between integrity, Provisional Comparison, and Certifying Comparison.
- Require independent trusted-current expected output for certifying claims.
- Treat a Presentation Self-Check, screenshot review, expected HTML, and Baseline Replay as non-certifying evidence.
- Label comparison state and limitations for the intended audience.

## Approval

- Confirm source licensing and permission to publish every factual and visual source.
- Obtain Country Office, regional, product-owner, and data-sharing approval appropriate to the audience.
- Confirm that policy meaning, caveats, uncertainty, and unavailable hazards are represented without false certainty.
- Record accountable approval for the exact immutable artifacts being released.

## Activation

Operational Warning/Alert activation additionally requires approved identity evidence, policy and registry releases, monitored authoritative retrieval, persistence/concurrency validation, recipient and provider controls, shadow/canary evidence, rollback procedures, and explicit send approval.

Failure of any applicable gate blocks publication or activation. Passing one gate never implies another.
